elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without Vendor consent
elements.evidence: The Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in interest by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the prior written consent of the Company

elements.element: Customer's consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: in no event may HDI assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Any change of control of the Company shall not ... give HDI any right to terminate

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement ... without the prior written consent of the Company (no free successor assignment for Vendor)
No notice mechanic appears; Customer assigns "without HDI's consent" with no notice requirement

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld

offending_extra_words: shall not constitute an assignment or
reasons: All atomic elements of the locked preferred level are met: Customer's consent-free affiliate and successor assignments, Vendor's consent requirement with a reasonableness standard, the competitor bar, and the no-termination-on-change-of-control protection.

Minimality fails: the insertion adds a deemed-assignment rule ("Any change of control of the Company shall not constitute an assignment") beyond the preferred position, which asks only that Vendor have no termination right on Customer's change of control.
Minimality also fails on the extra remedies "suspend or re-price", which are duplicated/expanded protection not required by the preferred position.
The 13-word anchor was expanded to 116 words; the same result could be achieved with a tighter insertion appended after the untouched sentence.
Intent is preserved: the original successors-and-assigns sentence remains effective, no undefined terms are introduced, and the added language does not contradict other commercial terms.
